title: Nigerian CV Format: The Complete Guide for 2026 (With Sample)
meta_description: The complete guide to Nigerian CV format: NYSC details, referees, what to include and avoid, plus a sample structure that wins interviews.
content_html:
Applying for jobs in Nigeria? Your CV needs to meet local expectations — and some of them differ from what international resume guides tell you. From NYSC (National Youth Service Corps) details to referee conventions, Nigerian employers look for specific information that a generic template won't include.

This guide covers the standard Nigerian CV format: what to include, what to leave out, the mistakes that get CVs rejected, and a complete structure you can follow today.

Quick answer: The standard Nigerian CV format runs two pages and includes: personal details, a professional summary, reverse-chronological work experience, education, NYSC details (year of service and place of primary assignment), skills, certifications, and 2–3 named referees with contact details. Unlike US resumes, Nigerian CVs expect NYSC information and on-page referees.

Key Takeaways

  • A Nigerian CV is typically 2 pages — not the strict one-page US rule.
  • NYSC details (year, place of primary assignment) are effectively mandatory for graduate roles.
  • Nigerian employers expect 2–3 named referees with contact details directly on the CV.
  • Leave out date of birth, state of origin, and passport photos unless specifically requested.
  • Nigerian job portals increasingly use ATS screening — keep formatting clean and machine-readable.

The Standard Nigerian CV Format

A Nigerian CV typically runs 2 pages (unlike the strict one-page rule common in the US). It follows this order:

  1. Personal details / header — Full name, phone number, email address, location (city and state), LinkedIn profile
  2. Professional summary — 3–4 lines summarizing who you are and what you offer
  3. Work experience — Reverse chronological, with achievements not just duties
  4. Education — Institutions, degrees, dates, grades where strong
  5. NYSC — Place of primary assignment, year of service (for graduates)
  6. Skills — Technical and soft skills relevant to the role
  7. Certifications — Professional qualifications (ICAN, CIPM, PMP, etc.)
  8. Referees — 2–3 referees with name, title, organization, phone, and email

What Nigerian Employers Expect (That Foreign Guides Miss)

NYSC details are effectively mandatory

For any graduate role, employers expect to see your National Youth Service Corps information: year of service, place of primary assignment (PPA), and discharge certificate number if relevant. Omitting it raises immediate questions. If you haven't completed NYSC, state your current status honestly (e.g., "NYSC: Awaiting mobilization, Batch B 2026").

Referees on the CV itself

While international guides often say "references available on request," Nigerian employers generally expect 2–3 named referees with contact details directly on the CV. Choose referees who will actually pick up the phone: former supervisors, lecturers, or professional mentors. Always inform them before listing them.

State of origin and date of birth: usually unnecessary

Older Nigerian CV conventions included date of birth, state of origin, and LGA. Modern practice — and most multinational employers in Nigeria — no longer require these, and including them can invite bias. Leave them out unless a specific job posting explicitly asks.

Passport photograph: only when requested

Some Nigerian job adverts still request a CV with a passport photograph attached. If the posting asks for one, include a professional headshot. If it doesn't ask, don't add one — it adds nothing and can trigger unconscious bias.

Writing Each Section Well

Professional summary (not "objective")

Skip the outdated objective statement ("To obtain a challenging position..."). Write a summary that states your profession, years of experience, 1–2 standout strengths, and what you're targeting:

"Customer service professional with 4 years' experience in telecoms, consistently rated above 90% CSAT. Skilled in complaint resolution, CRM systems, and team mentoring. Seeking a senior support role in fintech."

Work experience: achievements over duties

Don't just list what you were supposed to do — show what you actually accomplished. Compare:

  • Weak: "Responsible for handling customer complaints."
  • Strong: "Resolved 40+ customer complaints weekly, reducing average resolution time from 48 to 24 hours."

Start each bullet with an action verb, include numbers wherever possible, and tailor the bullets to the job you're targeting.

Education: lead with your highest qualification

List institution, degree, field of study, and graduation year. Include your grade only if it's strong (First Class, Second Class Upper, or equivalent). For HND/BSc holders, that's fine — list it confidently.

Common Nigerian CV Mistakes That Get You Rejected

1. The 5-page autobiography

Two pages is the sweet spot for most roles. If you're early-career, one strong page beats two padded ones. Cut religious activities, every seminar attended since 2015, and your primary school — none of them help.

2. Unprofessional email addresses

fineboy4life@yahoo.com or sweetmother123@gmail.com will get your CV binned. Use a simple firstname.lastname@gmail.com format.

3. Listing every skill under the sun

"Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, internet browsing, fast learner, team player, hardworking" — this tells the employer nothing. List skills relevant to the role, and be specific: "Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP)", "QuickBooks", "Python (pandas)".

4. Typos and inconsistent formatting

In a market where hundreds apply for each role, a CV with spelling errors signals carelessness. Proofread twice, then have someone else read it once.

5. Submitting a scanned image or photo of your CV

Some applicants photograph a printed CV and send the image. Applicant tracking systems can't read images — your application effectively doesn't exist. Always submit a proper PDF or Word document with selectable text. Test yours free to confirm it parses.

ATS Considerations for Nigerian Job Portals

Major Nigerian employers — banks, telecoms, multinationals — and job boards like Jobberman increasingly use applicant tracking systems. That means your CV must work for software and humans:

  • Use standard section headings (Work Experience, Education, Skills)
  • Avoid tables, text boxes, and graphics that break parsing
  • Mirror keywords from the job description naturally in your bullets
  • Submit as PDF with selectable text (not a scanned image)

Sample Nigerian CV Structure

ADAOBI OKAFOR
Lagos, Nigeria | +234 800 123 4567 | adaobi.okafor@email.com
linkedin.com/in/adaobiokafor

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Accountant with 5 years' experience in FMCG, ICAN-certified. Managed payables of ₦200M+ annually and cut month-end close from 10 to 6 days. Seeking a finance manager role.

WORK EXPERIENCE
Senior Accountant — Dangote Foods Ltd, Lagos | Jan 2021 – Present
• Reconciled supplier accounts worth ₦200M+ annually with 99.8% accuracy
• Automated expense reporting, saving the team 15 hours monthly
• Supervised 3 junior accountants

EDUCATION
B.Sc. Accounting — University of Lagos | 2016 – 2020 (Second Class Upper)

NYSC
National Youth Service Corps — PPA: First Bank, Ibadan | 2020 – 2021

CERTIFICATIONS
ICAN (ACA) — 2023

SKILLS
QuickBooks, SAP, Excel (advanced), Financial reporting, Tax compliance

REFEREES
Available with full contact details — or list 2–3 named referees here.

NYSC on Your CV: Getting It Right

The National Youth Service Corps section deserves special attention since foreign guides never mention it:

  • Format: "National Youth Service Corps — [State], [Year]–[Year]" followed by your Place of Primary Assignment on the next line.
  • What to highlight: If your PPA involved real responsibility — teaching, project work, community development (CDS) projects — give it 1–2 achievement bullets. "Led CDS group of 25 corps members to renovate 3 classrooms" is genuine experience.
  • Exemption/exclusion: If you're exempt (over 30 at graduation) or excluded, state it plainly: "NYSC: Exempted (graduated above age 30)." Don't leave a gap employers will question.
  • Still serving: "NYSC: Currently serving — PPA: [organization], [state] (completion [month year])." Many employers hire corps members nearing completion.

Where Nigerians Actually Find Jobs (2026)

  • Jobberman — Nigeria's largest job board; set up alerts for your target roles
  • LinkedIn — growing fast in Nigeria; optimize your profile with the same keywords as your CV
  • MyJobMag — aggregates listings across sectors
  • Company career pages — banks (GTBank, Zenith), telecoms (MTN, Airtel), and multinationals post directly
  • NYSC job portals — some employers recruit specifically from serving corps members
  • Referrals — as everywhere, the strongest channel. Tell your network you're looking.

Whatever channel you use, submit the same polished, ATS-tested CV. Verify it parses before you start applying — one check covers every portal.

Most Nigerian CVs rejected at the screening stage fail on missing NYSC details or absent referees — not on qualifications.

The majority of successful Nigerian job applications through major portals now pass through some form of automated screening first.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the standard Nigerian CV format?

The standard Nigerian CV format is a two-page document with: personal details (name, phone, email, city/state, LinkedIn), a 3–4 line professional summary, reverse-chronological work experience with achievements, education, NYSC details, skills, certifications, and 2–3 named referees with contact details. It differs from international formats mainly in the NYSC section and on-page referees.

Is NYSC required on a Nigerian CV?

For graduate roles, effectively yes. Nigerian employers expect your National Youth Service Corps details: year of service and place of primary assignment (PPA). Omitting it raises immediate questions. If you haven't completed NYSC, state your status honestly — for example, "NYSC: Awaiting mobilization, Batch B 2026."

Should I include referees on my Nigerian CV?

Yes. While international guides often say "references available on request," Nigerian employers generally expect 2–3 named referees with phone numbers and email addresses directly on the CV. Choose referees who will actually respond — former supervisors, lecturers, or mentors — and inform them before listing them.

How long should a Nigerian CV be?

Two pages is the standard for a Nigerian CV, unlike the strict one-page convention common in the US. Fresh graduates can sometimes fit on one page, but two pages is expected and accepted once you have a few years of experience. Keep every line earning its place.

Should I include my date of birth and state of origin?

No — modern practice in Nigeria no longer requires date of birth, state of origin, or LGA on your CV, and including them can invite bias. Most multinational employers in Nigeria don't want them. Leave them out unless a specific job posting explicitly asks.

Do Nigerian employers use ATS to screen CVs?

Increasingly, yes — especially banks, telecoms, multinationals, and job portals like Jobberman. That means the same ATS rules apply: single-column layout, standard headings, no text boxes or graphics, and keywords from the actual posting.
